reasons: The signal is already published: published_signal gives "P 11.13274 d, Rabtsevich, research note, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22967456". The published period agrees with fit_period_days 11.1327327 (fit_period_error_days 0.00001153) and with period_days 11.132794 to within 0.00005 d, so it is the same signal on the same star. A CTOI must be new, so I agree with the mechanical decision to drop.

The absence of a catalogue entry does not make it new: exofop_tois and exofop_ctois are empty and the verification record (2026-10-15 cross-match) finds no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match, but the research note reports the signal before this search, which is the condition for a drop.

For the record, the astrophysical evidence does not refute a planet, so the drop rests only on prior publication: pixel_verdict is "on target" in S32 (SNR 7.9) and S98 (SNR 19.9), both difference images centre the dip on the target star; triceratops_verdict is "likely planet" with fpp_mean 0.1715, nfpp_mean 0, most_likely_scenario "TP on TIC 4206066"; planet_radius_earth_radii 2.10 +/- 0.28; secondary_depth_ppm 26 +/- 61; odd_even_difference_sigma 1.13; gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.00965; transit_grazing False.

Cautions that a future reviewer of the published signal might weigh, but which do not change this decision: the caution "neighbour able to cause dip" lists five Gaia neighbours at 45-55" needing 34-83% dips, which the on-target difference images and nearby_scenarios_excluded True argue against; sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.00342 (depth_ppm_by_sector S98 1185 +/- 88, S6 862 +/- 118, S32 691 +/- 130), though cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.0739 is milder; stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 5.25 and fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.88 indicate a fit that is denser than the TIC star, which is consistent with the poorly constrained fit_impact_parameter 0.507 +/- 0.3070; joint_search_detected False (joint_search_snr 14.8 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 10.9) with the S6 and S32 single-sector SNRs 7.1 and 7.6 below expected 10.0 and 10.4.
No hold is warranted: released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification is empty, so no unused TESS data could change the fact that the signal is already reported.
